iPhone 5, 4S, 4, and 3GS with iOS 6 Information

Apple recently introduced the new iPhone 5. There are three key differences between the iPhone 5 and
earlier iPhone models that affect its integration in BMW vehicles.

1. The body of the new phone is thinner and longer compared to the iPhone 4/4S.

2. The iPhone uses a new 8-pin (Lightning) connector in place of the traditional 30-pin connector
used on all other iPhone variants, as well as iPod touch and iPod nano.

3. Elimination of the analog video signal.

The result is:
1. The iPhone 5 is not compatible with any of the current snap-in adapters available through
Aftersales.
The Plugin feature as a means of accessing one’s music library is not available on the iPhone 5.
(Customers are still able to access their music library using a USB cable; see details under
Question 3, “Will | need an adapter to use my iPhone5?”)
2. Watching videos stored on the device, on the car’s screen while parked, is no longer possible.

latest information.

audio files?
Yes.

e No, if you currently use an Apple “white cable” to connect your iPhone to your
vehicle.
In this case, all you need is the new Apple Lightning cable, included with your iPhone
5.
e Yes, if you currently use a Y-cable to connect your phone.

cable.
See “USB vs. Y-cable” on pages 3 and 4 to determine when a Y-cable is needed.

plug to the new 8-pin connector or “Lightning cable.”

BMW Automatic Start/Stop System Benefits and Operation

The Automatic Start/Stop (MSA) system is a further BMW EfficientDynamics measure aimed
at meeting BMW’s commitment to reducing CO2 emissions and enhancing fuel economy.

BMW, always a leader in innovative technology, will be the first automobile manufacturer to
bring MSA technology to all new models. MSA can improve fuel economy and reduce
emissions, since the engine is automatically turned off when the vehicle is stationary. All
manufacturers will eventually have to incorporate Automatic Start/Stop systems in their
vehicles to meet increasingly stringent emissions and fuel economy requirements.

Answers to some of the most common questions about MSA:

Q1. At times, the Automatic Start/Stop feature does not seem to shut off, while at other
times, it restarts the engine on its own without doing anything. Is this normal?

A1. Yes, the system controls the engine start/stop operation as needed to keep the vehicle’s
battery sufficiently charged, and maintain the set interior climate control temperatures.

Q2. Is it possible to turn off the system?

A2. Yes, this can be done manually via the Automatic Start/Stop function button. When
pressed, the LED is switched on, indicating that the start/stop function is deactivated.

Q3. Is it possible to permanently disable the start/stop feature?

A3. No, this system was designed to operate actively as a further measure by BMW to meet
its EfficientDynamics commitment to reducing greenhouse gases. However, at an owner’s

request, it is possible to modify this default active logic to “last user mode.”

With this logic, the current MSA’s activated or deactivated setting is stored after a vehicle
“power down,” and used on the next trip.

Note: All new BMW M models will have “last user mode” as the default setting from
production.

Apple recently introduced the new iPhone 5. There are three key differences between the iPhone 5 and
earlier iPhone models that affect its integration in BMW vehicles.

1. The body of the new phone is thinner and longer compared to the iPhone 4/4S.

2. The iPhone uses a new 8-pin (Lightning) connector in place of the traditional 30-pin connector
used on all other iPhone variants, as well as iPod touch and iPod nano.

3. Elimination of the analog video signal.

BMW Automatic Start/Stop System Benefits and Operation

The Automatic Start/Stop (MSA) system is a further BMW EfficientDynamics measure aimed
at meeting BMW’s commitment to reducing CO2 emissions and enhancing fuel economy.

BMW, always a leader in innovative technology, will be the first automobile manufacturer to
bring MSA technology to all new models. MSA can improve fuel economy and reduce
emissions, since the engine is automatically turned off when the vehicle is stationary. All
manufacturers will eventually have to incorporate Automatic Start/Stop systems in their
vehicles to meet increasingly stringent emissions and fuel economy requirements.

Answers to some of the most common questions about MSA:

Q1. At times, the Automatic Start/Stop feature does not seem to shut off, while at other
times, it restarts the engine on its own without doing anything. Is this normal?

A1. Yes, the system controls the engine start/stop operation as needed to keep the vehicle’s
battery sufficiently charged, and maintain the set interior climate control temperatures.

Q2. Is it possible to turn off the system?

A2. Yes, this can be done manually via the Automatic Start/Stop function button. When
pressed, the LED is switched on, indicating that the start/stop function is deactivated.

Q3. Is it possible to permanently disable the start/stop feature?

A3. No, this system was designed to operate actively as a further measure by BMW to meet
its EfficientDynamics commitment to reducing greenhouse gases. However, at an owner’s

request, it is possible to modify this default active logic to “last user mode.”

With this logic, the current MSA’s activated or deactivated setting is stored after a vehicle
“power down,” and used on the next trip.

Note: All new BMW M models will have “last user mode” as the default setting from
production.
